headline: A joint quality-and-diversity method for selecting reasoning rollouts
summary: An arXiv paper introduces PKTP, which selects partial reasoning rollouts by directly estimating the chance that at least one retained rollout will finish correctly. The authors report higher pass@k than a quality-only linear probe and a diversity-only selector across eight open-weight math-reasoning models, especially at moderate selection budgets. Their main setup samples 128 rollouts per problem, observes 4,000-token prefixes and keeps 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16; results average 20 repetitions of eight-fold cross-validation over roughly 600 filtered problems per model. Correctness is judged by Qwen3-32B answer equivalence. These are author-reported benchmark results, not an independent reproduction or evidence of end-to-end inference savings.
